findings.message: Factual claims verified against fetched excerpts: Nobel Prize facts page confirms 1903 Physics share, first person with two Nobels, and WWI mobile X-ray teams; Musée Curie confirms radiography cars predate 1905 and that Curie did not create them but worked to multiply them; Musée de la Grande Guerre confirms the 12 August 1914 War Ministry letters on training radiographers and listing existing apparatus plus her Red Cross radiography-service inspector role; AIP confirms redirected Radium Institute work, military radiology centers, vehicles equipped from late October 1914, and Irène as first radiological assistant at 17 (Nobel page confirms Irène's later Chemistry Nobel).

Card text aligns with the evidence: 'Radiography cars already existed. She did not invent them' and 'The War Ministry asked her about training radiographers and existing X-ray apparatus' match source excerpts without overreach; no lives-saved totals or X-ray-invention claims appear. The unsupported 'bullet before surgeon cut' card was removed per direction.

Contextual media is labeled honestly: Verdun, French field-hospital X-ray, Paris ambulances, Nice nurses and Western Front artillery clips all carry '(context)' or 'WWI context' labels and are not presented as Curie's own unit; Irène Curie 1917 trainee photo and mobile X-ray unit photo are genuine period subject images. No invented footage or titles.

Minor date inconsistency: the Irène Curie/Suzanne Veil file's Commons description guesses 1915 while the filename and video label use 'November 1917'; the label is defensible from the file title, but a relative 'c.1917' caption would be more cautious.

Keystone still carries 'Copyright undetermined' in its Commons permission template even though ShortName says Public domain (Missouri Historical Society open-access policy); acceptable with the MHS credit already present, but a documentary provenance note would strengthen the rights record.

Licenses and credits: all eight media items are Public domain per Commons receipts, each fully credited with author/collection, Commons Source URL and license; YouTube, Facebook and Instagram metadata all include full source list, per-item credits and licenses. Music 'Measured Paces' (Kevin MacLeod, incompetech, CC BY 4.0, ISRC USUAN1100164) is attested by the publisher catalogue and FAQ with visible attribution and monetized-use allowance; no Invented or Epidemic claims. Controller documented account scope and download evidence only; no extra provider permission is asserted beyond the CC BY 4.0 grant.

Narrative coherent for the 55 s silent card/clip arc: hook (wheels) → rise (Curie, Verdun, field X-ray, 1914) → turn (cars not her invention, multiplied with Irène and medical teams) → quiet break → reframe (science reaching people). Platform metadata descriptions and Instagram caption remain consistent with verified claims.
